title: Aspectual Periphrases
summary: Use começar a, continuar a, acabar de, deixar de, voltar a, vir a, and chegar a for subtle aspectual meaning.

sections.heading: Beginning, continuation, and interruption
sections.body: Portuguese uses verb phrases to show phases of an action. These choices often sound more natural than adding adverbs.

examples.en: We continue to follow the case.

examples.pt: Ele deixou de responder às mensagens.
examples.en: He stopped replying to the messages.

sections.heading: Resumption and recent completion
sections.body: **Voltar a + infinitive** means to resume; **acabar de + infinitive** means to have just done something. These are high-frequency structures.

examples.pt: Voltei a correr depois da cirurgia.
examples.en: I started running again after the surgery.

examples.pt: A loja voltou a funcionar normalmente.
examples.en: The store started operating normally again.

sections.heading: Outcome and unexpected extent
sections.body: **Vir a + infinitive** can suggest eventual outcome, often in formal style. **Chegar a + infinitive** emphasizes reaching an extreme or surprising point.

examples.pt: A proposta veio a ser aprovada meses depois.
examples.en: The proposal eventually came to be approved months later.

examples.pt: Ele chegou a trabalhar doze horas por dia.
examples.en: He even worked twelve hours a day.

examples.pt: O caso pode vir a mudar a lei.
examples.en: The case may eventually change the law.

keyPoints: Aspectual periphrases express phases and viewpoint of actions.
Acabar de means 'to have just done', not 'finish doing' in this structure.
Voltar a means resume or do again.
Vir a and chegar a are useful in formal narration and argument.

commonMistakes.note: Voltar requires a before the infinitive.

commonMistakes.right: Ele deixou de responder às mensagens.
